reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that yellow card issuance in soccer is not purely random but exhibits structured patterns—specifically underdispersion—suggesting referee consistency. The use of the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (CMP) distribution allows modeling of such data without assuming overdispersion typical in standard Poisson models. This enables detection of deviations from expected behavior, such as bias or temporal shifts. The referee consistency index (RCI) provides a scalar measure of this consistency by comparing mean to variance. Temporal bias detection uses pre/post-event data to identify changes in referee behavior, particularly relevant in the context of global disruptions like the pandemic. These primitives form a dual framework: one for static consistency and another for dynamic behavioral shifts.
